messages:
Sam: Quick thought — can we add an 'attenuation' primitive to runtime flags so a rollout can automatically reduce exposure when telemetry degrades?
Maya: Curious — how different from auto-pause / circuit-breaker?
Sam: It's related but finer-grained. Auto-pause stops traffic entirely. Attenuation gradually reduces percentage or per-cohort weight over time based on signals (latency, error-rate, model-quality).
Kevin: Example use-case?
Sam: Say a new config increases tail latency on some regions. Instead of cutting to 0, attenuation pushes cohorts 100% -> 80% -> 50% -> 20% over N minutes while we investigate. Gives graceful backoff and keeps partial capacity for quick debug telemetry.
Liz: UX question — in Console we'd need a slider or a timeline with clear rollback points. Also visible reason and triggered signal.
Maya: Telemetry gating is key — what signals should drive it? p95 latency, 5xx rate, NLU-quality drift. We should let teams wire custom signals too.
Kevin: Schema idea (rough):
```yaml
flag: new-routing-heuristic
attenuation:
  enabled: true
  metric: p95_latency_ms
  thresholds:
    - value: 150
      action: reduce_to 80
    - value: 250
      action: reduce_to 50
  window: 5m
  cooldown: 10m
```
Sam: We also need a safe default: attenuation only kicks in after N consecutive windows and only for cohorts < X% unless explicitly allowed. Don't want it to accidentally stall big launches.
Ruth: Ops-bot note: we should emit structured events when attenuation runs: {flag, cohort, old_pct, new_pct, reason, metric_value}. That makes audit + rollback easy.
ops-bot: [automated] deployment-check: attenuation feature toggles present in config schema, lint passed. :white_check_mark:
Liz: Console telemetry panel should show a mini-sparkline for the driving metric and an explanation: e.g., "p95 spiked to 210ms (threshold 150ms) — attenuated route weight 100->50%". Also allow manual override.
Maya: API surface: POST /flags/:id/attenuate to trigger manual attenuation; GET /flags/:id/attenuation for status. We already have override endpoints, this fits naturally.
Kevin: Backwards compatibility: flags without attenuation behave the same. For V1 we can make attenuation opt-in per-flag. Also add a dry-run mode where the control plane simulates attenuation and writes to audit log but doesn't change routing.
Sam: Good call on dry-run. Also add a 'recovery' path that can re-escalate exposure if metric improves, maybe a mirrored schedule (80->100) but with a longer time window.
Ruth: From SRE POV: add a global kill-switch at account/org level and rate-limits for attenuation frequency to avoid flip-flop.
Liz: UX copy: "Attenuation — automatically reduce exposure when a selected metric crosses thresholds. Learn more" with a link to runbook.
Maya: Runbook quick checklist draft: 1) confirm metric source 2) check population cohorts 3) check logs for root cause 4) if attenuation insufficient, escalate to full pause 5) postmortem if >30m.
Kevin: Implementation note — the router needs to accept fractional weights per cohort and an ephemeral override TTL. We have that already for canaries, reuse it.
Sam: Who wants to own the API PR + console work? I can do the API schema + backend hooks. Liz can take console mockups. Maya + Ruth will draft runbook and SLO constraints.
Liz: I'll mock tomorrow and post screenshots.
Maya: I'll start a small eval harness to simulate metric spikes and confirm attenuation schedule behaves.
Ruth: I'll add the kill-switch and alerting integration.
Sam: Great. One more: add a flag-level opt-out tag `no-auto-attenuate` for flags that must never be attenuated (billing, infra-critical).
Kevin: +1. Also add telemetry tags so we can query which attenuations happened across orgs.
Sam: Cool — I'll open the API RFC and link the mockups + runbook. Tagging @Liz @Maya @Ruth for follow-ups. :wave:
